$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
tests/test_manifest.py in this repository's own CI; `declared` is a statement
nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
IN PYTHON THE THING TO CHECK IS `[project.scripts]`, AND THAT IS NOT AN
ANALOGY. Go's manifests ask `go list` which main packages exist and Rust's
ask `cargo metadata` which binaries a workspace builds. Here the packaging
metadata IS the answer, and it is already a cross-repository contract:
stack-k8s's console.Dockerfile installs the Python tools by reading
`pyproject [project.scripts]`, and says so in a comment. So a script added
here without a manifest entry is a component the console image would install
and nothing would have declared.
TWO COMPONENTS, ONE SCRIPT. estate.json says this repository runs `verdryx`
and `verdryx-drift`. There is one console script and six subcommands:
`verdryx-drift` is the ROUTINE name for `verdryx drift`, the same shape as
idryx-detect and qryx-trend.
THE EXIT CODE FOR A MISSING ARGUMENT IS argparse's 2, AND IT IS DECLARED
BECAUSE A ROUTINE READS IT. stack-up's routine treats a non-zero exit as an
error to show an operator, so the difference between `you did not give me a
baseline` and `the drift check failed` is a cross-repository fact and not an
implementation detail. mockryx and qryx one repository over use 1 and 2 to
mean different things again; nothing makes these three agree, and this file
at least makes each one say which it is.
distribution: not published: installed from the repository with pip (git+https); no PyPI package yet

the_console_image_installs_it_by_reading.why: stack-k8s's console.Dockerfile copies this repository in and installs the script its packaging metadata names. stack-up does the same into its own venv. Neither reads this file, which is why the check below compares the manifest against pyproject rather than against either of them.

it_is_the_scheduled_half.why: stack-up runs it as a routine and stack-k8s as the quality-drift CronJob. The name in estate.json's `runs` is the routine's, not a script's, which is why it maps to a subcommand here.
